claims: Artemis I launched on November 16, 2022.
Artemis I was a successful uncrewed test flight of SLS rocket and Orion spacecraft orbiting the Moon.
Artemis II is scheduled to launch on April 1, 2026.
Artemis II has a duration of ~10 days.
Artemis II is a crewed lunar flyby.
Artemis II is the first crewed flight of Orion to test systems beyond low Earth orbit.
Artemis II crew will fly around the Moon using a free-return trajectory.
Artemis II will splash down in the Pacific Ocean.
Artemis II is aimed at testing Orion’s life-support systems.
Artemis III is targeted for mid-2027.
Artemis III is a crewed lunar landing.
Artemis III will use SpaceX or Blue Origin landers.
Artemis III will land the first woman and first person of color on the South Pole.
Artemis IV is targeted for early 2028.
Artemis IV is a lunar landing.
Artemis IV is focused on bringing international crew to the Gateway station and the surface.
Artemis V is targeted for late 2028.
Artemis V is a lunar landing.
Artemis II will lift off from NASA's Kennedy Space Center (LC-39B).
Artemis II launch day includes liftoff, insertion into Earth orbit, and systems check.
Artemis II includes Translunar Injection where Orion performs a critical engine burn to leave Earth orbit for the Moon.
Artemis II days 2-4 involve journey to the Moon.
Artemis II days 5-6 involve lunar flyby passing within ~4,100 miles of the lunar surface using a slingshot gravity maneuver.
Artemis II days 7-10 involve return to Earth, atmospheric re-entry, and splashdown.
Artemis IV-V are scheduled annually from 2028.
Launch dates are subject to change based on technical readiness including evaluation of the Artemis I heat shield and Artemis II system testing.
